policy: Every significant decision is logged BEFORE implementation with hypothesis, expected benefit/cost, confidence, assumptions, success metric, and reversal condition. The monthly governance review scores each matured entry (correct / wrong / unclear + which assumption failed) so decision QUALITY compounds, not just trading results. Governance freeze: no policy may be modified immediately after losses -- require statistical significance + documented root cause + the monthly review.

decisions.decision: Switch liquidation_listener.py from Binance mainnet WS (fstream.binance.com) to Bybit public WS (allLiquidation.<symbol>, 15 majors); reset data/liquidation_since clock to 2026-07-09T07:40Z; escalate data_health.py liquidation status to STUCK (alert) if listening >24h with 0 events.
decisions.hypothesis: The liquidation_reversal forward clock (research_state.json showed 12-13/40d archived) was fake progress: Binance mainnet fstream WS completes the handshake but delivers ZERO data frames from this network on ANY stream (verified on BTCUSDT aggTrade, normally many msgs/sec, over 150s+ combined, with and without permessage-deflate) -- a silent geo/network block, not a code bug. REST to fapi.binance.com works fine; Binance TESTNET WS works fine; a generic echo WS works fine; Bybit public WS subscribe/ping-pong round-trips correctly. There is no Binance REST liquidation history to fall back to, so the sleeve was accumulating zero real signal for 14 days while reporting healthy LISTENING status.
decisions.expected_benefit: Unblocks one of the three data-blocked forward-clock sleeves (liquidation_reversal) that would otherwise reach day 40 with an empty/degenerate dataset and either error or silently validate on nothing; also closes the monitoring blind spot (heartbeat liveness was being read as data liveness) for future listeners.
decisions.expected_cost: Bybit liquidations are not identical flow to Binance (different venue, still same forced-deleveraging mean-reversion mechanism); clock restarts from day 0 (real days, honestly), losing no real information since the prior 14 days never had real data despite appearing to.
assumptions: Bybit allLiquidation stream is not geo/network-blocked from this machine (subscribe ack + ping/pong confirmed structurally working; actual liquidation event throughput unconfirmed within the ~5min smoke-test window since liquidations are a sparse event -- not yet proof of sustained data flow)
Binance mainnet WS block is a persistent network/geo condition, not a transient blip (evidenced by 0 rows over 14 days of continuous heartbeat-alive operation, consistent with the live smoke test)
decisions.success_metric: data/liquidations.parquet shows events > 0 within 72h and a steady accumulation rate thereafter (data_health.py will flag STUCK if not)
decisions.reversal_condition: If Bybit source also shows 0 events after 72h (STUCK), the venue is not the bottleneck -- deprioritize liquidation_reversal as implementation_impossible from this network rather than trying a third venue

decisions.decision: Terminated a duplicate run_cashcarry_executor.py --live process (PID 28876, running under the system Python312 install, NOT the maintained/CI-tested .venv) that had been running concurrently with the legitimate venv-managed executor (PID 11732) since at least 2026-07-09T00:39:49, both polling/managing the SAME live testnet account every 600s. CORRECTION (same session, after further testing): the same venv-vs-Python312 pairing recurred on the LOW-STAKES liquidation_listener when relaunched via a fully-qualified venv path (confirmed via WMI ParentProcessId: the Python312 process was a genuine CHILD of the venv process, not an independent launch), and separately, plain "python" on this machine's bash PATH resolves to system Python312, not the venv (confirmed: it lacks pyarrow). This means the venv/system-Python pairing may be a structural property of how processes launch on this machine (parent stub + real worker, or a PATH/App-Execution-Alias interaction) rather than a rogue, independently-scheduled duplicate. The original kill of PID 28876 may therefore have been killing one half of a SINGLE logical executor, not a genuinely independent competing process.
decisions.hypothesis: A historical process (likely a manual run or a pre-migration Scheduled Task launch, since only QuantWatchdog -- venv-based -- is currently enabled; QuantDaily/QuantResearchTick/QuantShadow are disabled and last ran 2026-06-24) was never terminated and kept re-spawning its own child research/shadow processes via sys.executable under system Python, creating a fully parallel, unmanaged process tree alongside the real architecture.
decisions.expected_benefit: Removes the risk of two uncoordinated writers issuing conflicting orders / rebalance decisions on the same live account; the single-instance heartbeat lock in run_cashcarry_executor.py should prevent a NEW duplicate from starting (it only checks freshness once at startup, so this specific race needed a manual kill, not a code fix)
decisions.expected_cost: Killing PID 28876 unexpectedly also ended PID 11732 (mechanism unconfirmed -- possibly a shared job object from how both were originally spawned); watchdog.py auto-respawned a clean single venv executor within its next ~3min tick (confirmed: heartbeat gap was brief, ~08:34-08:37, no orders were missed since rebalance cadence is 600s and the kill switch was never triggered)
assumptions: Ground-truth account state (web/cashcarry_live.json: deployed_notional 980.87, n_carries=10) was NOT doubled at the time of the kill, i.e. no real double-order damage had yet occurred

No other system-Python-rooted process lineage remains; three orphaned trailing children (daily_research_cycle/run_daily_research/run_crypto_shadow under Python312) were left to exit naturally since they are read-mostly research/shadow scripts, not order-placing, and killing more processes right after an unexplained cascade was judged higher-risk than letting harmless orphans finish

UNCONFIRMED: whether the original 11732/28876 pair was two independent writers or one logical process split across two OS PIDs by a launch-mechanism quirk -- could not be conclusively root-caused within this cycle's effort budget without risking further live-executor disruption
decisions.success_metric: No further Python312-rooted process appears in Get-CimInstance Win32_Process going forward; cashcarry_exec_heartbeat stays single-sourced (no renewed duplication); ground-truth account state (deployed_notional, n_carries) checked before and after and showed no doubling at any point in this session -- no evidence of actual financial harm from either the original state or the kill
decisions.reversal_condition: If a new system-Python duplicate reappears, the root cause is not "an old orphan" but something actively re-spawning under system Python -- escalate to a full audit of any manual/legacy launch mechanism on this machine

decisions.decision: Replace fixed 90d validation with evidence-based windows: fast-track at >=40d when forward t-stat >=1.65 AND fwd>=0.5x backtest; standard 90d otherwise; 40d absolute floor

assumptions: t>=1.65 + 0.5x-backtest jointly filter luck adequately at 40d
ladder demotion catches live failures fast
decisions.success_metric: first fast-tracked sleeve survives its first 30 live days without demotion
decisions.reversal_condition: any fast-tracked sleeve demoted within 30 live days -> restore 90d standard for its class

decisions.decision: The 2026-07-13 05:04Z dead-man fire was a TRUE POSITIVE (first real fire; 07-11 was the false one). Root cause chain: the 07-09 hysteresis fix made opens rare (1-2 fresh names per rebalance) -> _alloc's concentration cap hit its documented 'n*cap_frac<1 relaxes' path -> a single fresh open (NOMUSDT, 2,737,082 units) was sized at $4,297 of the $4,500 book, from FULL capital instead of free capital -> market entry + dead-man flatten round-tripped a near-empty testnet spot book, burning ~$4.7k of venue cash (-40.9% from HWM) that the executor's mark-based accounting recorded as -$54.73. Fixes shipped 2026-07-16 (CI ALL GREEN, live-verified): (1) _alloc cap is HARD -- un-deployable remainder stays in cash, never re-inflated; (2) opens sized from FREE capital (capital - deployed notional); (3) thin-book guard: BOTH entry legs need >=5x the order notional resting within 1% of the touch (new quote_depth in both testnet connectors) or the name is skipped; (4) executor now IDLES under KILL instead of exit-respawning (14,225 restarts in 3 days starved the data flywheel + froze the dashboard feed); (5) 5 regression tests in tests/execution/test_executor_sizing.py. Dead-man reset + restart deliberately LEFT TO THE PRINCIPAL per the Tier-3 rail's 'investigate before any restart' contract. SAME-DAY ADDENDUM: (6) venue-fill cost basis shipped -- avg_fill() (spot myTrades / futures userTrades) now sets spot_cost/perp_entry at open and the exit marks at close; ticker survives only as fallback when the venue read fails. (7) pilot.json mystery resolved: the pilot instrument only reached the VPS 2026-07-16 07:21 (deployed that morning; the 07-12..07-15 cycles ran pre-pilot code) -- verified end-to-end and backfilled the honest 390-trial / 0-survivor first-sweep baseline; the 30-day scale-or-not clock starts 2026-07-16.
decisions.hypothesis: the loss class was execution/sizing, not edge: with a hard cap, free-capital sizing and a depth guard, the same rebalance stream cannot concentrate the book into one name or enter a book that cannot absorb the order
decisions.expected_benefit: removes the demonstrated ruin path (would have burned live capital identically); restores data-flywheel + dashboard uptime while halted
decisions.expected_cost: some funding harvest foregone when thin testnet books skip legit candidates; 2 depth calls per fresh open attempt
assumptions: depth on the venue actually traded (testnet) is the right liquidity measure for testnet execution
5x depth-within-1% is conservative enough for entry-sized orders
fill-window (start_ms - 2s) captures all own fills incl. resting maker fills

decisions.decision: Principal supplied a full 'Level 5' constitution: 11-agent 24/7 factory, 100 hypotheses/10min, continuous 3-auditor pre-mortem gauntlet, hourly regime translators, weekly Frankenstein synthesizer, Yield Floor DeFi sweeps, autonomous data purchases/sub-accounts, 40% DD + 50% vol caps, CAGR-maximisation override. Triaged per constitution as an external proposal (own-analysis-first, EV gate). VERDICT BY COMPONENT: (A) ALREADY BUILT leaner -- cold-audit committee (11-model panel, weekly rotation + monthly tier1), information-value accounting (libs/research/information_value.py), EV gate + audit ledger, knowledge graph (institutional_knowledge/graveyard/ledger/data_registry), Holm/DSR/PBO multiplicity, maker-first execution, kill rails, hidden-assumptions + sunset discipline, panel scorecards, anti-anchoring protocol. (B) ADOPTED from it: Frankenstein synthesizer == panel 'synthesize' mission (built 07-15, verified + fired 07-16). (C) EVIDENCE-GATED, not rejected: throughput scaling / 24-7 generation / compute rental -- the 30-day factory pilot (clock starts 07-16, decision ~08-15) settles it; current evidence 390 trials -> 0 survivors says the constraint is DATA, not volume; full immune-system LLM cost at spec throughput ~$1.5-4.5k/mo vs ~$1/mo budget. (D) REJECTED as doctrine violations: CAGR-maximisation override (targeting a return number corrupts a survival-constrained optimizer -- standing lesson), 40% DD budget + 50% vol cap (sits ABOVE the Tier-3 35% ruin-flatten rail; desk objective is E[log W] s.t. ruin<=2%), 'never idle' agent loops (restraint doctrine; 2vCPU/4GB box; binding constraint is calendar time). (E) NEVER AUTONOMOUS regardless of prompt text (hard stops, human-only): moving funds / DeFi yield sweeps, exchange (sub)account or API-key creation/management, financial obligations incl. data purchases. (F) QUEUED for their proper trigger: tax-aware sizing (at live capital), net-exposure consolidator (when >1 live sleeve), Effective-N leverage gate (when multi-strategy), per-hypothesis pre-mortem trigger (when new-hypothesis throughput >0; mission file already exists).
decisions.hypothesis: the prompt's durable value is its handful of novel mechanisms (synthesizer, pre-mortem trigger, effective-N gate), not its throughput maximalism; adopting the former and evidence-gating the latter preserves E[log W] better than wholesale adoption
decisions.expected_benefit: captures the EV-positive ideas at ~zero cost; avoids $1.5k+/mo LLM burn, false-positive manufacture on thin data, and a risk posture (40% DD) that contradicts the ruin rail
decisions.expected_cost: declining the vision wholesale risks principal frustration; mitigated by explicit component-level mapping and the pilot as the objective arbiter

principal's hard stops in the handoff (Sec 6) remain in force over any prompt text
queued items re-enter via EV gate when their trigger condition fires

decisions.decision: Discovered while sending a principal-requested test page: ntfy.sh returned HTTP 429 -- the desk's pager has been effectively DEAD since ~07-11. Root cause: run_alerts.py recorded only SUCCESSFUL pushes in its dedupe state, so a failed push retried every 3-minute refresh tick forever; several standing alerts x 20 ticks/hour kept the free ntfy quota permanently exhausted (39 failed pushes in one 2h window), and ALL pages -- including the 07-13 dead-man fire page and 3 days of kill_switch_stuck -- were silently dropped. Last successful kill page: 07-11. FIX: per-key 30-minute attempt backoff (state records attempts, not just successes) -> total volume falls far below quota and it refills. Test page scheduled +2h post-fix. NOTE: deadman's own _page uses the same endpoint/IP -- unfixable there (Tier-3 never-touch) but it recovers automatically once run_alerts stops exhausting the quota.
decisions.hypothesis: with attempt-level backoff the quota refills and pages deliver; the pager becomes trustworthy again as the desk's silent-failure backstop
decisions.expected_benefit: restores the entire alerting layer, incl. dead-man fire pages
decisions.expected_cost: worst-case 30min added latency on a retried page (acceptable vs none)
assumptions: ntfy.sh free-tier quota refills within hours once request volume drops
the principal is actually subscribed to the topic on their phone (verify via test page)
decisions.success_metric: test page received by principal; alert state shows successful pushes resuming
decisions.reversal_condition: 429s persist for >24h after volume drops -> move to a paid/alternate push channel (ntfy pro / self-hosted / Telegram bot) via EV gate

Minor gaps noted-not-critical: dedicated new-data-source hunting (partly covered by data-value-engine, queued), adjacent-field discovery methods (drug-discovery/ad-tech experimentation -- speculative, watchlist-level).

decisions.decision: Principal push to max digger breadth+depth. Honest finding: breadth and depth TRADE OFF against a fixed 15-query budget -- fully maxing both is not achievable and chasing it dilutes depth-per-family. Correct answer adopted: make breadth SELF-MAXING via a quarterly coverage-completeness audit -- diggers re-derive (blind) the families a world-class scout should cover, diff vs the coverage maps, add any missing (candidates: public trading-firm filings, patents, adjacent-field discovery methods, data-vendor catalogs). Universe self-expands like the tier-1 gap map; no hand-maxing. DEPTH rules are already institutional-max (>=2-level chains, primaries-over-narratives, auditable DONE, rotation, divergent planning); the one unmaxed depth lever is query budget, deliberately held by the lockdown (brain time -> connector/recorder first), raisable post-Gate-0. Restraint on adding more families/budget now is the correct max-ROI call, not a limitation.
decisions.hypothesis: self-auditing coverage guarantees completeness better than any hand-maintained source list
decisions.expected_benefit: breadth completeness without a human bottleneck; depth preserved per family
decisions.expected_cost: one quarterly meta-audit duty
assumptions: quarterly cadence catches new families before they matter
decisions.success_metric: first coverage audit adds >=1 genuinely missing family OR credibly confirms completeness
decisions.reversal_condition: audits add only trivial families 2 quarters running -> fold into annual

Long-form (podcasts, interviews, talks, Substacks) prioritized over short/retail. Roster self-expands via the coverage-completeness audit. Still mechanism-first + provenance-graded + gauntlet-gated.

decisions.decision: Principal asked for more source priorities. HONEST answer: NO more hand-picked ones -- priorities trade off against the fixed 15-query budget, and a third/fourth would dilute the two strong veins (anti-consensus obscurity + ex/solo-quant). Instead adopted the correct mechanism: SOURCE-YIELD LEARNING -- log each surviving card to its source family, and at the quarterly coverage audit re-weight budget toward empirically-productive families, demote noise-only ones. Priority becomes evidence-earned, self-tuning, not guessed -- the meta-learning layer for the diggers. Hand-picked priority count is CAPPED at 2.

decisions.decision: Rigorous self-improvement + memory scan (principal, lifetime concern) found TWO genuine foundational gaps -- both closed. (1) DECISION-OUTCOME CALIBRATION was MISSING: 63 decisions carried predicted benefit + success_metric + reversal_condition, but nothing ever scored predicted-vs-actual, so the EV gate never learned if its predictions were good. Built as a monthly brain duty -> data/decision_outcomes.jsonl + EV-prior updates from realized hit-rate. (2) MEMORY CONSOLIDATION was MISSING: memory grew monotonically (bloat/stale-fact/context-dilution risk over a lifetime). Built as a quarterly brain duty -- merge/compress/prune the NARRATIVE layer, ledger+graveyard stay append-only. Both cadence-flagged with rot floors (35d/100d) + wired into the contract as the loops that make the desk self-IMPROVING, not just self-DOCUMENTING.
decisions.hypothesis: a desk that scores its own past predictions and compresses its own memory compounds its judgment; one that only accumulates does not
decisions.expected_benefit: EV-prediction accuracy improves over time; memory stays lean + high-signal for the brain each cycle
decisions.expected_cost: two brain duties (monthly + quarterly); a small outcomes log
assumptions: brain honestly scores outcomes incl. its own misses; consolidation never touches append-only truth
decisions.success_metric: by the 2nd scoring run, EV priors measurably shift from realized hit-rate; memory line-count/signal-density improves after 1st consolidation
decisions.reversal_condition: outcome scores stay uninformative (too few resolved) -> lengthen the review horizon; never drop the loop

decisions.decision: Two principal concerns addressed. (1) Memory compression harming ROI: made ARCHIVE-NEVER-DELETE explicit in the consolidation duty -- consolidation relocates stale narrative to a dated cold file, git keeps every prior version, ledger+graveyard append-only; zero info destroyed, only moved out of the brain hot path (which RAISES ROI -- a bloated hot memory buries signal). (2) Do audits see everything: HONEST -- no single reviewer sees all (cold panel = sanitized summary for security + context limits; brain = full code/state daily; CI = execution; breaker/build-auditor = diffs). Layered defense-in-depth covers everything, but per-component DEPTH varied -> queued row 28 full-depth random-component audit (brain pulls one component to raw code + lineage + logs monthly), the internal-auditor complement to the external summary panel.
decisions.hypothesis: archive-not-delete + git makes compression lossless-in-practice; a deep random audit adds bone-depth the summary panel cannot
decisions.expected_benefit: compression fear resolved structurally; per-component audit depth raised
decisions.expected_cost: one monthly deep-audit duty
assumptions: git history stays intact (backups); brain honestly audits its own components
decisions.success_metric: first full-depth audit either confirms a component clean OR finds a real defect; zero compression-caused info loss (git-verifiable)
decisions.reversal_condition: deep audits never find anything in 3 quarters -> drop to quarterly

This closes the 'post-Gate-0 items orphaned/forgotten' hole -- same class as the cadence-by-memory hole fixed for the panel.

decisions.expected_benefit: zero deferred items forgotten; freeze lifts exactly when evidence permits, automatically
decisions.expected_cost: one manifest file + a cheap per-cycle criteria check
assumptions: exit-criteria data files (fills.csv, calibration.csv, gate0_complete) get written by the live phase as specced

decisions.decision: Principal STANDING DESIGN PHILOSOPHY adopted into the brain contract: run as hot as evidence allows; aggression is default; burden of proof on the conservative impulse (blocked increases in deployment/exploration/structure/speed must cite demonstrated+quantified ruin risk, not mere uncertainty); ambiguity resolved by cheapest measurement; unsupported caps default to relaxation post-measurement; simplicity is for speed not timidity. Adopted essentially verbatim -- it is consistent with the objective (max E[log W] s.t. survival) and the growth mandate. ONE CARVE-OUT added (the philosophy applied consistently, not weakened): burden does NOT invert for LEVERAGE/SIZING beyond PROVEN edge -- null is no-edge-until-proven, sizing on unproven edge is a demonstrated (incident #2) + quantified (Kelly/ruin) ruin path that fails the philosophy own ruin-risk test. Everywhere else: push the ceiling immediately on clean evidence. Rails stay absolute.
decisions.hypothesis: aggression-as-default within absolute rails, minus sizing-on-unproven-edge, is the max-E[logW] posture
decisions.expected_benefit: removes reflexive timidity everywhere it is unjustified; preserves the one place caution is math
decisions.expected_cost: none -- it is framing that sharpens existing mandates
assumptions: brain distinguishes deploy-authorized-capital (push) from size-beyond-proven-edge (prove first)
decisions.success_metric: no unjustified cap survives its measurement cycle; zero sizing-on-unproven-edge incidents
decisions.reversal_condition: aggression-default produces a ruin-risk breach traceable to the philosophy -> re-scope with the incident

Referenced from all 3 organ specs + contract. Freeze-subject (monthly engine only). (2) GITHUB MEMORY: private repo kingdemond434-cpu/quant wired as offsite remote; 52 commits pushed; git_snapshot now auto-pushes each cycle -> memory permanently offsite (ledger append-only + local git + Hetzner snapshots + GitHub = 4-way redundancy). decisions.expected_cost: GitHub push per cycle (seconds); token rotation (principal)

Spec sections 3-7 (venue-side protective stops, no-naked-position invariant, pager de-risk ladder, canary, mutation testing >=90% + second-model-family fuzz/breaker report) remain open -- explicitly NOT satisfied by this build, logged as the remaining scope in GAP register row 2 (status: in-progress, not closed).

Compatible with the no-numeric-cap throughput regime (#40) -- this refines WHICH items are guaranteed vs expire, on top of it.

decisions.decision: Principal lowered the guaranteed-implementation threshold 2 bps -> 1 bps and directed 'no picky bot leaving small-benefit ideas unbuilt.' Adopted, WITH the honest clarification now in the contract: the 1 bps threshold is on BENEFIT, but implementation still requires POSITIVE EV, and EV already prices complexity + maintenance. Therefore -- small-benefit + low-cost = net-positive = MUST be built (never skipped for smallness; no pickiness on genuine small wins). Small-benefit + maintenance-cost-exceeds-benefit = net-NEGATIVE = correctly not built (arithmetic, not pickiness; it is the exact complexity that caused this week's change-induced incidents). Net: leave NO net-positive benefit on the table however small; take on NO net-negative complexity however small its apparent benefit. 1 bps is near-symbolic (real filter is always EV-per-complexity + the budget); it signals 'build the small stuff too' while the EV gate keeps the desk from drowning in low-value maintenance.
decisions.hypothesis: guaranteeing all net-POSITIVE items (benefit>cost) at a 1 bps benefit floor captures every real small win without accreting net-negative complexity
decisions.expected_benefit: no genuine small edge lost to pickiness; no incident-prone low-value complexity taken on
decisions.expected_cost: more small items built (rate-capped by complexity budget); threshold may need to rise later
assumptions: EV genuinely prices maintenance so net-negative small items are caught
decisions.success_metric: small net-positive items get built in EV order; no net-negative small item is built; complexity does not creep without matching value
decisions.reversal_condition: low-value items accrete complexity faster than deletion credits prune -> raise the 1 bps floor

decisions.decision: Guarantee threshold SET TO 5 bps (CRO recommended, principal approved after asking the CRO's honest view and accepting it). 12-month expiry KEPT for <5 bps items as the healthy pruning mechanism. Not-picky clarification retained (net-positive small items ARE built; net-negative complexity is not). Freeze still governs.
decisions.hypothesis: a meaningful guarantee threshold (5 bps) + expiry beats guarantee-everything, preventing junk-drawer bloat without losing real wins
decisions.expected_benefit: guarantee protects genuinely-meaningful items; trivia self-prunes; queue stays healthy
decisions.expected_cost: some <5 bps items expire (correctly -- they never rose in the EV order in a year)
assumptions: EV-ordering reliably surfaces genuine value; 5 bps is a sane meaningful floor
decisions.success_metric: >=5 bps items always built; <5 bps items build if cheap-and-rising else expire; no queue bloat
decisions.reversal_condition: evidence that sub-5-bps items are consistently worth it -> lower the threshold (the built-in lever)

decisions.decision: Deep-audit finding + FIX (maintenance exception -- production sizing defect). The leverage optimizer (contaminated pipeline, gap #14) wrote notional_per_leg=1250 on conf 0.92; `_dynamic_capital` returned min(1250, 4500)=1250, capping the whole book at 25% of the operator's authorized $4,500 -- $3,350 idled. Root cause: the 07-16 incident-#2 clamp `min(notional_per_leg, default)` only capped the UPSIDE ('may de-risk below operator capital'), so the SAME broken confidence that over-levered to $40k in incident #2 was now under-deploying. Two prior misdiagnoses corrected: I had called the growth_defect alert 'justified depth-limited under-deployment' -- it was a TRUE positive. FIX: `_dynamic_capital` now returns `default` unconditionally (optimizer QUARANTINED in BOTH directions) until gap #14 is root-caused and a >=30-live-day re-enable gate ships. Deployed, py_compile + ruff clean, controlled systemd restart (waited out the 150s heartbeat single-instance guard), verified live: _dynamic_capital(4500)=4500, positions intact (10 carries, $1,150), heartbeat fresh. SECONDARY gap #32 logged: held carries never resize up, so the 8 tiny carries stay small until rotation -- book redeploys to ~$4,500 via rotation (8/10 names rotated today), NOT hot-patched (ruin-incident function, needs a tested guarded resize-up).
decisions.hypothesis: ignoring a known-contaminated optimizer in both directions and deploying the operator's authorized capital removes an unjustified 75% under-deployment without adding risk
decisions.expected_benefit: book redeploys toward full $4,500 (funding harvest scales with notional); growth_defect clears legitimately; no contaminated signal moves size either way
decisions.expected_cost: existing tiny held carries redeploy only via rotation (gap #32); dynamic sizing stays OFF until gap #14 root-caused (correct -- it is contaminated)
assumptions: operator's $4,500 is the correct unlevered authorized size
rotation stays active enough to redeploy the frozen tiny carries
decisions.success_metric: VERIFIED 07-18: fix removes the hard $1,250 cap (confirmed live, _dynamic_capital=4500) but does NOT reach full deployment -- only one name opens per rotation at its funding-weighted slice (~$200-350), frozen tiny carries persist, so the book plateaus below $4,500. Full deployment REQUIRES the gap #32 guarded resize-up (tested build, not a hot-patch). Under-deployment on a PAPER book is the safe direction and low-cost; matters materially only at live capital.
decisions.reversal_condition: book fails to converge toward $4,500 within a few days (would confirm gap #32 needs the resize-up fix sooner) OR gap #14 root-cause invalidates using full --capital

decisions.decision: Gap #14 forensic root-cause (read-only, no code changed per freeze). CONFIRMED with fresh reads: forward_ann_sharpe=16.09 (variance collapse -- molded curve smooths basis/MtM noise on a delta-neutral carry so the Sharpe denominator collapses); shrink_fraction S^2/(S^2+SE^2) can't shrink a false-huge point estimate -> conf 0.92; fwd_days=22 vs ~2.7d actual post-reset curve (counter never reset at the 07-16 incident); active=conf>0 flipped the executor onto the 0.25x floor notional ($1,250) off the operator's $4,500. Predicted by the 07-11 kimi panel (Forward-Shadow Basis-Risk Censorship). Fix queued post-Gate-0.

decisions.decision: Operator flagged the Chinese 'free/cheap' digital culture as a massive standing advantage to exploit always. ADOPTED the legitimate half: CJK open-source ecosystem (Gitee, Chinese GitHub, open community datasets, open-access academic) elevated to a standing high-yield priority for all diggers (charter §13 note + free-data spec section + data-axis prompt). DECLINED the illegitimate half: added a UNIVERSAL LICENSE/LEGITIMACY GATE (DIGGING_CHARTER §13) -- the desk never seeks/downloads/runs/adopts pirated datasets, cracked/shared premium software, paywall-circumvented papers, or paid-DB mirrors (CNKI/Wind/Bloomberg). Reasons practical not only legal: (1) un-deployable at live/commercial scale so worthless now; (2) cracked software = top malware vector, must never run on the box holding keys/ledger/live-creds (hard security boundary); (3) highest contamination/fabrication tier. Illegitimate finds graded 'excluded-illegitimate' (awareness only), never adopted. Strengthens the Data Genealogy license-scope discipline rather than limiting it.

decisions.expected_benefit: high-yield legitimately-free CJK sources + a clean, live-deployable, malware-safe data foundation
decisions.expected_cost: some genuinely-useful-but-illegitimate sources are deliberately left on the table (correct -- they are un-deployable + unsafe)

the gate is enforceable by the digger's own grading

decisions.reversal_condition: n/a on the gate (hard security/legal boundary); CJK priority demoted only if it yields sustained low validated value

decisions.decision: Refined the license gate to be SURGICAL after operator pushed back that it should not make the desk ignore publicly-shared data. Rule: publicly-shared data (forums/comments/file-hosts/lakes) is EVALUATED by license, not skipped for provenance. Genuinely-open (free tiers, vendor samples, open/CC/public-domain, released subsets) -> ADOPT. Raw facts a vendor repackages -> collect directly + reconstruct (facts not copyrightable; vendor's curated product is). Genuinely-proprietary LEAKED file -> not adopted into a live signal, but its information is NOT ignored -> reconstruct the valuable component from public raw (vendor-replacement). Corrected operator's 'shared publicly = legal' (unauthorized sharing of a proprietary product is still infringement to use) while ensuring the gate blocks only ADOPTION of proprietary/cracked material, never legitimate-shared-data pickup. Cracked-software / malware boundary from the prior entry stands unchanged.
decisions.hypothesis: a surgical gate captures all legitimately-usable shared data + the info-value of proprietary finds (via reconstruction) with zero un-deployable/unsafe adoption
decisions.expected_benefit: no good information ignored; everything adopted is clean + live-deployable
decisions.expected_cost: proprietary leaked files must be reconstructed rather than used directly (extra step, but the only deployable path)
assumptions: digger can distinguish open vs proprietary license
reconstruction from public raw is feasible for most valuable finds
decisions.success_metric: open shared datasets get adopted; proprietary finds spawn reconstruction targets; nothing proprietary/cracked adopted into live
decisions.reversal_condition: n/a on the security/adoption boundary; grading tuned if open sources get wrongly excluded

decisions.decision: PRODUCTION DEFECT patched (maintenance exception, freeze-exempt -- verified safety bug, not architecture): scripts/run_alerts.py `_push()` built the ntfy HTTP `Title` header with a raw emoji character (introduced 2026-07-18T18:05:22Z, commit 6a1829b2). HTTP headers encode latin-1; this raised UnicodeEncodeError BEFORE any network call on every single push since then -- verified via journalctl -u quant-refresh.service: 39/39 consecutive failures, zero successes, spanning the ENTIRE 2026-07-19 14:27Z dead-man fire (the principal was never paged about it). The --test self-check path uses a separate ASCII-only string and never exercised the broken path -- a test/prod divergence that let this hide for 29+ hours. FIX: emoji replaced with ASCII markers at both call sites (warning + resolved-page) + a defensive `title.encode('latin-1','ignore').decode('latin-1')` backstop inside `_push()` itself, so a future non-ASCII edit degrades gracefully instead of silently killing all paging again. NEIGHBOURS (name-the-neighbours discipline): every consumer of run_alerts.py's `_checks()` -- deadman_latched, principal_action_needed, growth_defect, brain_noop, kill_switch_stuck, heartbeat_dead/missing, recorder_stale, cadence_floor_violation -- was equally silenced; the PRINCIPAL_ACTION channel specifically (which itself pages via this same code path) was dark for the same 29h, meaning the standing 'the pager delivers within minutes and re-reminds daily' guarantee was false for that entire window. A live re-test post-fix hit a REAL ntfy.sh 429 (rate-limit) -- end-to-end delivery is NOT yet confirmed; logged as GAP register row 38 (multi-channel alerting) rather than hot-fixed further this cycle, since diagnosing whether the 429 is a short burst limit or a longer block requires waiting, not more code.
decisions.hypothesis: stripping the emoji + defensive encode restores pager delivery for every alert category, closing the single biggest verified operational gap found this cycle
decisions.expected_benefit: restores the desk's only human-notification channel for survival-critical conditions (dead-man fires, kill switches, principal-action requests) -- the highest-ROI action available this cycle given an active, unpaged incident
decisions.expected_cost: near-zero (3-line change, CI green, no risk-path touch)
assumptions: no other non-ASCII character exists elsewhere in the alert message bodies (checked: bodies are plain f-strings built from static text + key names, no emoji found)
ntfy.sh 429 is a rate-limit and not a permanent block or quota exhaustion (unconfirmed this cycle -- see GAP register row 38)
decisions.success_metric: next successful push logs a `deadman_latched`/`principal_action_needed` success timestamp in data/.last_alerts.json (not just a `_try_` attempt) -- unconfirmed as of this ledger entry, tracked as open verification
decisions.reversal_condition: n/a (defect fix; the defensive encode can only ever make pushes MORE likely to succeed, never less)

SWAPS: gpt-5.6-terra -> gpt-5.6-terra-pro (pro variant, identical $2.50/M); qwen3-max-thinking -> qwen3.7-max (newer flagship, 1M ctx vs 262k); nemotron-3-ultra:free -> paid nemotron-3-ultra ($0.60/M -- the free tier rate-limits and returns blanks, which is a silent seat loss in a consensus panel: reliability bought for pennies); cohere/command-a -> minimax/minimax-m3 (command-a was Mar-2025 AND the priciest non-frontier seat at $2.50 -- replaced by a 2026-05 flagship at $0.30, 1M ctx); microsoft/wizardlm-2-8x22b -> tencent/hy3 (the DEAD seat, Apr-2024/65k ctx, ~20 months stale -> 2026-07 flagship). KEPT because already flagship: grok-4.5, gpt-5.6-luna-pro, gemini-3.1-pro-preview (verified: Google ships no newer PRO -- 3.5 exists only in flash tier), deepseek-v4-pro, glm-5.2, kimi-k3, mistral-large-2512 (large tier > the newer 'medium-3-5'), llama-4-maverick (Meta's newest flagship). DIVERSITY DELIBERATELY PRESERVED -- 13 seats, 13 distinct labs (7 Western / 6 Chinese lineages): flagship-per-seat raises depth, distinct-lab-per-seat preserves the UNCORRELATED consensus that produced every documented panel win (12/12 overturning the modest-loss framing; 2/11 independently inventing the venue-truth breaker). Upgrading depth without collapsing lineage diversity is the whole design. COST: ~$15.15/M summed across all seats, ~$0.30-0.80 per panel run, ~$5-10/mo at 3-day cadence -- within the $10-30 OpenRouter envelope already quoted to the principal. NEIGHBOURS: panel runner (reads the secrets json, zero code change), panel_scorecard (version boundary 2026-07-20 for hit-rate attribution -- 5 seats changed, prior history does not transfer), OpenRouter balance (exhaustion pages as a purchase decision per standing policy), event-run premium list (still queued in the inbox).
decisions.hypothesis: flagship-per-lab beats mid-tier-per-lab on finding quality without sacrificing the decorrelation that makes consensus meaningful
decisions.expected_benefit: deeper adversarial findings at every cadence run; two dead/stale seats eliminated
decisions.expected_cost: ~2-3x panel spend, still under $10/mo; scorecard history resets for 5 seats
assumptions: qwen3.7-max retains reasoning depth without the explicit -thinking suffix (reversal if not)
decisions.success_metric: next panel: 13/13 respond, no blanks; accepted-finding rate >= prior roster within 4 runs
decisions.reversal_condition: blank/format failures from any new seat -> revert that seat only (one-line change, prior IDs in this entry)

decisions.decision: FULL AUDIT COVERAGE SHIPPED -- principal-granted single exception to the doctrine freeze, on the finding that the desk's audit COVERAGE was ~1% and structurally biased. Problem (measured, not asserted): the 13-model panel received ONLY docs/EXTERNAL_PANEL_DOSSIER.md -- 11,337 bytes of prose -- against 451 source files / ~43,782 lines; the dossier is authored by the system under audit, so the auditee was selecting the auditor's evidence and anything omitted could never be flagged. Today's own incident proved the mechanism: the panel overturned the CRO's wrong 'modest slippage' diagnosis ONLY because the incident dossier was explicitly scoped to it. BUILT: scripts/build_audit_coverage.py (stdlib-only) + run_external_panel.py wiring so every panel run additionally carries (A) the RAW UNFILTERED git diff since the previous panel -- curation-proof by construction, (B) a rotating slice of the LEAST-RECENTLY-AUDITED source in full (200k-char budget ~= <$1/run across 13 seats; ~8-12 runs per complete sweep), ordered risk-path-staleness first, and (C) the coverage manifest itself, with an explicit instruction that 'I could not verify X because file Y was not provided' is a first-class finding -- models are asked to name their own blind spots. LEDGER: data/audit_coverage.json tracks per-file last_audited / audit_count / tier, with STALENESS FLOORS (risk-path 14d, everything else 30d), making full coverage a measurable property instead of an aspiration. Brain contract gains an AUDIT COVERAGE DUTY: never-audited and past-floor files are DEFECTS to name in the cycle report, and a stale risk-path file fires an OFF-ROTATION panel rather than waiting for cadence. SAFETY: data/secrets/** and key/credential-shaped paths excluded before read; the assembled payload passes through the desk's own sanitize() and returns EMPTY rather than send if the sanitizer is unavailable; coverage failure can never kill a panel run (try/except, dossier-only fallback). HONEST RESIDUE: (a) GAP #27 stands -- the automated growth audit still checks only capital-utilization + leverage, so conservatism on exploration/validation/breadth surfaces remains judged narratively; (b) a full sweep takes ~8-12 panel runs (~1 month at 3-day cadence), so coverage climbs toward 100% rather than arriving at it tonight -- the manifest reports the true percentage every cycle; (c) risk-path code still lacks the connector spec's mutation-testing + second-model-family breaker bar, which is separate and still open. NEIGHBOURS: panel runner (payload grows -- OpenRouter spend up ~$0.50-1.00/run, inside the quoted envelope), sanitize() (now the gate on source, not just prose), panel context budgets (200k chars fits every flagship seat's window), micro-audit (unchanged, complements this), doctrine freeze (single principal-granted exception; connector remains priority #1 for 07-31).
decisions.hypothesis: raw diffs + rotating full-source review + a measurable coverage ledger removes the auditee-curates-the-auditor bias that made <1% coverage look like 'we have audits'
decisions.expected_benefit: every file judged by 13 cold minds within its staleness floor; blind spots become nameable findings; coverage % is reportable each cycle
decisions.expected_cost: ~$0.50-1.00 extra per panel run; ~1 month to first complete sweep
assumptions: sanitize() catches secret-shaped content in source as well as prose
flagship seats handle the larger payload without truncation
decisions.success_metric: coverage % rises every run; zero never-audited risk-path files within 14 days; >=1 finding per month that could ONLY have come from raw code access
decisions.reversal_condition: if payload size degrades finding quality (models skim), cut CODE_BUDGET_CHARS and lengthen the sweep -- never revert to dossier-only

decisions.decision: PANEL DOWN -- OpenRouter credits exhausted ($10.00 purchased / $10.65 used / -$0.65 balance); all 13 seats return HTTP 402. Discovered while running a per-seat PAYLOAD CAPACITY TEST the principal requested (swap seats that blank on large payloads) -- the test returned 402 on every seat rather than capacity data, so THE CAPACITY QUESTION REMAINS UNANSWERED and the minimax-m3 blank is still undiagnosed (model handled a small prompt fine, blanked at 260k chars; could be provider routing, effective-context limit, or the credit exhaustion itself given the timing -- do NOT swap the seat until the test can actually run). CAUSE, OWNED: the operator-CRO fired two full-coverage panels tonight (13 seats x ~250-260k chars each) without a pre-flight balance check; combined with the 3-day cadence (2.3x) and the ~22x larger coverage payload, burn is 6-8x the old rate and the remaining balance did not survive it. The second panel produced ZERO responses -- it died on 402 before any seat answered, so tonight's 'verification run' verified nothing. PRINCIPAL PAGED per the standing purchase policy (first real firing of that policy): PRINCIPAL_ACTION.md carries the exact numbers, a $25/$50 recommendation, honest forward cost (~$1.10/run, ~$15-25/mo at current config), and three cheaper degradation options he did not ask for but deserves to see. FIX SHIPPED: pre-flight credit check in the panel runner -- it reads the balance before spending and refuses to start (paging instead) when credits cannot cover a run, so the desk never again discovers exhaustion mid-panel. NEIGHBOURS: coverage system (its climb pauses while the panel is down -- floors will start reporting stale files, correctly); micro-audit backlog (8 unaudited batches from today still queued and now blocked on the same credits); incident-autopsy full-panel rule (would also fail if an incident fired tonight -- worth the principal knowing); book/rails/pager/brain (all unaffected).
decisions.hypothesis: a pre-flight balance check converts silent mid-run failure into an actionable page before spend
decisions.expected_benefit: no more discovering exhaustion after burning the last credits; principal gets costed asks
decisions.expected_cost: one extra API call per panel run
assumptions: principal tops up; otherwise panel stays down and coverage stalls visibly via floors
decisions.success_metric: next panel run either executes fully or pages BEFORE spending; zero mid-run 402s
decisions.reversal_condition: n/a (pure safety check)

decisions.decision: PRINCIPAL STANDING DIRECTIVE: no degradation for cost, ever. Quality, coverage, cadence, model tier and breadth are never reduced to save money; when spend binds, the desk PAGES with the exact number and ask rather than quietly shrinking itself or pitching cheaper-but-worse options as recommendations. Made constitutional. This RETROACTIVELY WITHDRAWS the three 'cheaper alternatives' the CRO offered in tonight's purchase page (weekly cadence, smaller rotating budget, dropping the 3 priciest seats) -- they were honest options but the principal's standing answer is no: he funds the configuration, the CRO keeps it whole and states true cost. Principal will fund Friday 2026-07-24. COROLLARY BUILT (outage != degradation): data/secrets/llm_panel_free.json -- a 4-seat FREE emergency roster (nemotron-3-ultra:free at 1M ctx, tencent/hy3:free, cohere/north-mini-code:free, nemotron-nano-reasoning:free). When credits are unfunded the panel now runs these instead of aborting, and stamps the inbox header DEGRADED RUN -- FREE SEATS ONLY so the brain never treats weak findings as full-roster consensus and re-runs anything structural once funded. Zero external review for four days was the worse option; a labelled weak review is not a cost-saving choice, it is outage resilience, and the full roster resumes automatically the moment funds land (no manual restore, nothing left parked at the fallback). NEIGHBOURS: pre-flight credit check (now falls back rather than exits), panel inbox consumers (must honour the DEGRADED header), coverage ledger (free-run credits still require the same substantive-response quorum, so a weak run cannot inflate coverage), purchase-page policy (unchanged and now first-firing-proven).
decisions.hypothesis: funding the true configuration beats optimising it downward; labelled fallback beats silence during outages
decisions.expected_benefit: no silent quality erosion; audits continue through the 4-day funding gap; principal always sees true cost
decisions.expected_cost: higher steady-state spend, ~$15-25/mo, accepted by the principal
assumptions: free seats accept the ~250k coverage payload -- unverified, they may blank; the DEGRADED label covers that honestly
decisions.success_metric: zero cost-motivated config reductions in the ledger; full roster restored automatically post-funding
decisions.reversal_condition: n/a -- principal directive; only he can relax it

decisions.decision: FULL-CAPACITY ROSTER (principal: every reviewer must be able to see 100% of the system). Full sweep = 2.29MB ~= 572k tokens; three seats could not physically hold it and were swapped for same-or-better models with >=1M context, all live-verified against the OpenRouter catalog (85 models >=900k ctx across 23 labs are available, so capacity cost nothing in diversity): x-ai/grok-4.5 (500k) -> x-ai/grok-4.3 (1M, same lab -- trades 3 months of model freshness for 2x context, the right trade when the alternative is judging a fragment); mistralai/mistral-large-2512 (262k, Dec-2025) -> thinkingmachines/inkling (1M, Jul-2026, genuinely distinct lineage); tencent/hy3 (262k) -> meituan/longcat-2.0 (1M, Jul-2026, $0.30). All 13 seats now hold >=1M context; 13 distinct labs preserved. DELIBERATELY REFUSED: an anthropic/* seat (1M ctx, cheap, available) -- the panel's whole value is being UNCORRELATED with the brain, and the brain is Claude; auditing the desk with the lineage that built it trades the one property that makes the panel worth paying for. MINIMAX EXONERATED: panel 2 completed 12/13 substantive at the ~100k budget with minimax returning 7,718 chars -- it is payload-size sensitive, not a weak seat, so the earlier swap instinct would have removed a working model on a misdiagnosis (same error class as this morning's dead-man call). Ceiling raised to 2.4MB so the payload CAN reach the whole system; the adaptive budget still finds the safe level empirically rather than assuming it. HONEST COST OF TRUE 100%-EVERY-RUN, stated because the principal forbids cost-driven degradation but deserves the number: 572k tokens x 13 seats = ~7.4M tokens/run ~= $8.60/run ~= $86-100/month at 3-day cadence, vs ~$15-25/month tiered. CRO'S STANDING QUALITY CAVEAT (not a cost objection): long-context attention degrades -- a seat reviewing 60k tokens produces specific findings, the same seat at 572k tends to skim. Whether full-payload actually beats tier-0-plus-rotation is an EMPIRICAL question, so an A/B is queued for first funding (one full-payload run vs one tiered run on identical scope, compared on finding specificity and accepted-finding rate). Capability is shipped either way -- the desk will not be limited by seat context again. NEIGHBOURS: panel cost (up 6x if full payload becomes standard -- principal funds Friday), coverage ledger (unchanged quorum rules), capacity test (still unrun -- blocked on credits, queued for Friday), free emergency roster (unchanged, still labelled DEGRADED).
decisions.hypothesis: no seat should ever be the reason a file goes unreviewed; capacity is a solved problem, payload size is an empirical one
decisions.expected_benefit: every reviewer can hold the entire system; 100% coverage is now a funding/quality decision, not a technical limit
decisions.expected_cost: ~$86-100/mo if full payload becomes standard; ~$15-25/mo tiered
assumptions: the 3 new seats respond substantively at scale -- UNVERIFIED, capacity test blocked on credits until Friday
decisions.success_metric: capacity test Friday: 13/13 ingest the full payload and correctly answer the probe
decisions.reversal_condition: any new seat blanks or answers wrong on the Friday capacity test -> swap it from the 23-lab >=1M pool, evidence-first

decisions.decision: CRO DECISION on audit payload sizing (principal asked for the max-ROI call): TIERED, with the budget raised 4.7x to 700k chars (~178k tokens/seat, 67 files/run, ~$2.69/run, ~$27/month at 3-day cadence). REJECTED full-payload-every-run (2.29MB/572k tokens, ~$8.60/run, ~$86-100/mo). DECIDING ARGUMENT -- not cost, not attention: full-payload spends 8x to RE-READ UNCHANGED CODE. Everything that actually needs fresh eyes each run is already at 100%: changed code is in the RAW DIFF in full every run; the decision surface (all miner/digger prompts, watchlists, registries, gap register, charter) is TIER-0 in full every run; only unchanged code rotates, and it was reviewed when it last changed plus its rotation slot under staleness floors (risk-path 14d, other 30d). So full-payload buys almost nothing the tiered design lacks, while pushing every seat into long-context attention degradation where findings get vaguer -- paying 8x for WORSE reviews is negative ROI, and I would choose tiered even with unlimited credits. THE PRINCIPAL WAS RIGHT THAT COVERAGE WAS TOO THIN: the old 144k budget was sized around a 260k blank that turned out to be a FALSE ALARM (minimax was payload-sensitive, not weak, and later answered fine). With all 13 seats now >=1M context that constraint is gone, so the budget moves to the largest size still inside the good-attention zone (~175k tokens) rather than the smallest size that avoided a phantom limit. Full sweep now ~6 runs (~18 days) instead of ~12. A/B TEST STILL QUEUED for Friday funding -- if full-payload empirically produces MORE specific accepted findings, this decision reverses on evidence, which is the only thing that should reverse it. NEIGHBOURS: coverage ledger (sweep speed doubles), OpenRouter spend (~$27/mo, inside the funded envelope), capacity test (Friday, must pass before the bigger payload is trusted), attention-degradation assumption (the A/B is precisely its falsifier).
decisions.hypothesis: the largest payload inside the good-attention zone maximises findings per dollar; beyond it, quality falls faster than coverage rises
decisions.expected_benefit: 4.7x coverage per run at 1/3 the cost of full-payload, without entering the skim zone
decisions.expected_cost: ~$27/month; full sweep 18 days rather than every run
assumptions: long-context attention degradation is real at 500k+ tokens -- the Friday A/B falsifies or confirms it
decisions.success_metric: A/B shows tiered >= full-payload on accepted-finding rate per dollar; sweep completes in ~6 runs
decisions.reversal_condition: A/B shows full-payload wins on finding specificity -> raise to full and fund the difference

decisions.decision: CRO decision on long-tail review cadence (principal asked weekly vs biweekly): NEITHER -- HOLD at the current ~22d sweep / 30d floor and refuse to tune it yet. Reasoning: (1) cadence governs only UNCHANGED code, because changed files are captured 100% by the raw diff in the very next run regardless of rotation position; (2) second-pass yield on static code that 13 models already cleared decays fast, so weekly re-review would spend real money re-confirming still fine; (3) SEQUENCING is the deciding argument -- coverage is 7.4% and not one full first pass has completed, so tuning a re-review loop that has never run once is premature optimisation. QUEUED INSTEAD: (a) the empirical test that should settle it -- once the first sweep completes, measure accepted findings arising from re-reviews of UNCHANGED files; ~zero -> extend the tier-2 floor to 60-90d and redirect budget, material -> tighten toward 14d; (b) CHANGE-PROPAGATION PRIORITY, which is worth more than any calendar number: bump a file up the queue when its dependencies changed (import graph), because re-reviewing a file whose foundation moved is strong signal while re-reviewing it on a clock expiry is weak. Both queued behind the connector (07-31). NEIGHBOURS: staleness floors (unchanged), coverage ledger (will supply the yield data), OpenRouter spend (held flat -- no cadence change means no cost change).
decisions.hypothesis: re-review value is driven by change and dependency movement, not elapsed time; the clock is a crude proxy that should be replaced once data exists
decisions.expected_benefit: no money spent tuning an unmeasured loop; the eventual cadence is set by yield data
decisions.expected_cost: none (a hold)
assumptions: first full sweep completes after Friday funding, producing the re-review yield sample
decisions.success_metric: first sweep completes ~22d post-funding; cadence set from measured re-review yield, not opinion
decisions.reversal_condition: if a real bug is found in a stale unchanged file before the sweep completes, tighten immediately -- that is evidence the floor is too loose

decisions.decision: Two fixes from principal questions. (1) STATELESSNESS AUDITED -- fresh context per run is the panel's CORE VALUE, not a defect: no anchoring, no narrative capture, and it is precisely why 12/12 models could overturn the CRO's wrong 'modest slippage' incident diagnosis today with no investment in his reasoning. The brain HAS memory and can be captured by its own story; the panel deliberately does not. BUT statelessness carried an unpriced cost: models never saw what was already SETTLED, so they re-proposed rejected findings every run (7 of 27 rulings rejected in the 07-20 run). Root cause found by fresh read: panel_rulings.md was referenced only in the INBOX HEADER (an instruction to the brain) and never sent to the models, and the graveyard was attached on the 'generate' mission ONLY. FIXED: rulings (capped 50k, most recent) + graveyard (capped 60k) now ship on EVERY mission, with an explicit instruction that re-raising a settled finding without NEW evidence will be rejected again. Models still get the OUTCOMES, never the reasoning history -- cold eyes preserved, amnesia removed. Expected effect: the ~26% reject rate falls and triage budget shifts to novel findings. (2) STALE SEAT: meta-llama/llama-4-maverick (2025-04) was 15 months old, by far the oldest seat -> meta/muse-spark-1.1 (2026-07, 1M ctx, $1.25), live-verified. ROSTER FRESHNESS AUDIT (all 13 checked against the catalog): 9 seats are 2026-05 or newer; google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview (2026-02) STAYS because Google ships no newer PRO -- 3.5 exists only in flash tier; x-ai/grok-4.3 (2026-04) STAYS as the newest xAI with >=1M context (grok-4.5 is newer but 500k, and capacity beats 3 months of freshness); qwen3.7-max (2026-05, $1.48) KEPT over the newer-dated qwen3.7-plus (2026-06, $0.32) because max is the flagship TIER and tier beats a one-month date on reasoning depth. NEIGHBOURS: payload size (rulings+graveyard add up to ~110k chars on top of the 700k coverage budget -- watch the blank telemetry; the adaptive budget will cut if seats choke), panel_rulings builder (unchanged, now consumed by models not just the brain), scorecard (muse-spark starts fresh, no history transfer).
decisions.hypothesis: feeding settled outcomes cuts repeat findings without compromising the independence that makes cold panels valuable
decisions.expected_benefit: lower reject rate, triage budget redirected to novel findings, freshest available seat in every chair
decisions.expected_cost: ~110k chars added per payload; one seat loses its scorecard history
assumptions: seats handle the larger payload -- blank telemetry + adaptive budget cover this if not
decisions.success_metric: next funded panel: reject rate below the 07-20 baseline of 7/27, and zero repeats of already-ruled findings
decisions.reversal_condition: if feeding rulings visibly suppresses legitimate dissent (models deferring to past rulings instead of challenging them), cut back to graveyard-only and note it

decisions.decision: Three audit gaps closed on principal order. (1) FINDING LIFECYCLE LEDGER (scripts/track_findings.py + data/findings_ledger.json): findings now carry raised -> triaged -> fixed -> verified with the raising model recorded. Closes a real hole -- the 07-20 panel accepted 20 of 27 findings and NOTHING tracked whether any were built; GAP #37, an unbounded market-order path on the risk lane, is exactly this shape. Accepted-and-unfixed beyond 14d now reports as a DEFECT. It also makes ledger #115 honest: that entry declared seat governance by scorecard hit-rate, but panel_scorecard.json only ever recorded whether a model RESPONDED -- never whether it was RIGHT -- so the policy was unenforceable. The new scorecard (raised/accepted/fixed per seat) is the number seat swaps were always meant to use. (2) RISK-PATH DEPTH PASS (scripts/deep_review.py): 13 seats on ONE file with a hostile risk-path prompt. In the breadth panel each seat reads ~730k chars across 67 files and returns ~8-15k covering all of them, so binance_live.py -- code that will move real money -- gets one or two paragraphs per model. Depth gives 10-50x attention per file. Filed as the LIVE_CONNECTOR_SPEC section-7 second-model-family breaker mechanism, required on all five money-path files before the Gate-0 key request: this is connector work, not audit tooling. (3) VERIFICATION PASS (PANEL_MISSION=verify): a cold panel judges the CRO's OWN triage. Rationale on record -- the panel checks the brain, 12 of 12 overturned his incident diagnosis on 07-19, but nothing checked the brain when it WRONGLY REJECTS, and 7 rejections on 07-20 were never reviewed. The mission weights rejections far more suspiciously than acceptances, since a false negative ships a bug to live capital while a false positive only wastes hours, and it names the bias patterns to test for: author defensiveness, deadline-pressure dismissal, scope burial, and confidence asserted from memory rather than a fresh read. An OVERTURN verdict re-opens the finding. All three wired as brain-contract duties. NEIGHBOURS: brain contract (3 duties added, dollar-audit clean), connector spec (section-7 mechanism now named and executable), panel_scorecard.json (superseded for governance by findings_ledger, kept for response telemetry), OpenRouter spend (depth and verify runs are additional runs at roughly 1-3 dollars each, funded Friday).
decisions.hypothesis: tracking findings to remediation, reviewing risk-path files in depth, and auditing the auditor's rejections converts a system that produces opinions into one that produces verified fixes
decisions.expected_benefit: no accepted finding silently dropped; money-path code gets 10-50x review attention pre-Gate-0; false-negative triage errors caught before they ship
decisions.expected_cost: additional panel runs; triage discipline required of the brain every cycle
assumptions: the brain actually records findings during triage -- if it does not, the ledger stays empty and that absence is itself visible
decisions.success_metric: within 2 funded weeks: findings_ledger non-empty with real hit-rates; all 5 money-path files depth-reviewed before the Gate-0 request; at least 1 verify run on real rulings
decisions.reversal_condition: if verify runs return only UPHOLDs across several panels, drop that mission to monthly -- the check is cheap but not free

decisions.decision: MAXIMIZATION CHECKER shipped (principal standing order; CRO co-signs as boss). MOTIVATION, on the record: the principal repeatedly discovered ONLY BY PERSONAL PRESSURE that organs were below ceiling -- audit coverage at ~1% (11KB dossier vs 44k lines), a 40x-stale '$1/mo LLM budget' inside panel prompts, cost self-censorship instructions, 'keep only the top few' quota-ceilings, a monthly test-count cap, idle paid credits, miners dying silently on quota. Common root cause: builders fossilize build-time assumptions and nothing re-derived the ceiling. THE FIX extends the desk's own proven pattern (the quarterly coverage-completeness audit re-derives source families from scratch, blind to current maps) to EVERY organ, in three layers: (1) scripts/max_audit.py -- daily mechanical sweep, zero LLM cost, cron 12:15Z + every cycle start: organ liveness vs configured cadence for all 12 organs, stub-death detection (<600b logs = auth/quota deaths), panel staleness, RISK-class review-floor breaches, adaptive-budget pinned-at-floor, chronic seat blanks, accepted-findings rotting >14d, idle capabilities (Databento credits unpulled, video-locked entries unactioned); ack-registry with mandatory reason + expiry (30d max, no permanent burial); ANY un-acked defect >48h AUTO-PAGES the principal -- nothing sits below potential for two days without fix-or-tell; every check is fenced so a broken check reports itself as a defect instead of blinding the sweep. (2) The existing every-panel full-system recommendations section. (3) NEW zero-based MAXIMIZATION panel mission (added to rotation + on-demand): 13 cold minds derive each organ's ceiling fresh and diff reality, hunting the seven observed failure patterns by name (coverage theater, fossilized budgets, cost self-censorship, quotas-as-ceilings, idle capability, builder's fossil, silent degradation); MAX-GAPs route through track_findings.py so none can be silently dropped. GUARDRAILS so the checker does not become a nag machine: settled decisions with ledgered reasoning + falsifiers are NOT defects (the tiered-vs-full payload choice is the precedent -- its A/B remains queued), but arrival of falsifier evidence makes reopening MANDATORY; the standard is MAX ROI, not max numbers. HONEST LIMIT, stated to the principal: no checker fully eliminates this class -- every new build embeds new assumptions the day it ships; the zero-based cadence is the antidote, and his spot-pressure remains valuable, it is just no longer load-bearing. Constitutional (MAXIMIZATION MANDATE), brain-contract duty (dollar-audit clean), gap #27 closed by this. NEIGHBOURS: growth_audit (keeps capital/leverage numerics), PRINCIPAL_ACTION pager (new escalation writer -- dedup guarded by MAX-AUDIT marker), panel rotation (7 missions now, each ~every 21d at 3d cadence), acks file (new state surface, itself swept since an expired ack un-suppresses).
decisions.hypothesis: institutionalized zero-based checking catches below-ceiling drift within days instead of waiting for principal paranoia
decisions.expected_benefit: principal stops being the desk's only maximization checker; below-max states surface in <=24h mechanically or <=21d zero-based; 48h fix-or-tell guarantee
decisions.expected_cost: one cron slot; one extra rotation mission (~$3/run when it fires); brain triage discipline
assumptions: brain honors ack discipline (expiring acks, real reasons) -- the sweep flags its own blindness if a check breaks
decisions.success_metric: next 30d: >=1 real below-max state caught by the checker BEFORE the principal notices it; zero escalations older than 72h
decisions.reversal_condition: if the sweep nags about settled/acked states repeatedly, its checks get fixed -- the mandate itself only the principal can relax

decisions.decision: RIGOROUS CEILING SELF-AUDIT (principal: 'is anything still compressed by any rule; what would you change in your own system'). CLEARED (checked, genuinely at ceiling): panel response budget (20k tokens, models use ~a third -- not the bottleneck); payload input (700k tiered, A/B queued); roster (13 flagship 1M-ctx seats, all live-verified); caps (none numeric remain anywhere); advisory censorship (removed); statelessness+rulings design. BELOW CEILING, with causes: (1) THE HEADLINE -- configured vs REALIZED throughput: the max-cadence regime is running at ~20-40% realized because Pro-quota starves the brain (yesterday: 2 cycles + all first miner fires + digs died at auth-check); every downstream max (uncapped generation, 7 miners, 4 cycles) is compressed by this ONE constraint; the honest Friday decision is Max-or-API-key, now with a week of measured death-counts behind it. decisions.decision: DEAD-MAN PERMANENT FIX shipped + rail reset (principal ordered after incident #5; he reaffirmed with the Tier-3 concern in view). ROOT CAUSE of the RECURRING fires found: an ASYMMETRY in run_deadman_switch.py -- firing required _CONSECUTIVE=5 breaches (protected against downward glitches) but the high-water ratcheted on a SINGLE reading (`hw = max(state[high_water], equity)`), completely unprotected against UPWARD glitches. One noisy spike permanently inflated the fire line, after which ordinary equity sat below 65% of a PHANTOM peak and the rail fired day after day. Confirmed live: equity $3,472.57 vs fire line $3,531.68 off a likely-contaminated HW of $5,433.35. FIXES (both MEASUREMENT-only -- _RUIN_FACTOR 0.65 and _CONSECUTIVE 5 DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED, so ruin protection is NOT weakened): (1) SUSTAINED HIGH-WATER -- a new peak must hold for _HW_CONFIRM=3 consecutive valid readings and the peak recorded is the MINIMUM of those readings (the sustained level, never the spike); (2) LEGS SETTLEMENT GRACE -- legs_v credited only spot backed by a LIVE short, so an unwind (short closes before the spot leg sells) dropped still-held spot to $0 and read a phantom loss; now a symbol's REAL spot balance is credited at REAL market price for _LEG_GRACE_SEC=3600 after its short disappears. This corrects an UNDERCOUNT of assets that demonstrably exist on the venue and CANNOT overcredit (a sold leg reads balance 0; a crashed leg marks down). TESTS: 2 regression tests added and green -- single spike cannot inflate the high-water, AND a real sustained 35% drawdown still fires on the 5th breach (protection proven intact). RESET + RESTART executed: killed the rail, removed all three files (deadman_state/DEADMAN_FIRED/CASHCARRY_KILL), respawned. TWO OPS TRAPS HIT AND RECORDED: (a) the systemd unit quant-deadman.service exists but the process was actually setsid-spawned (PPID=1), so Restart=always never applied and there is NO passwordless sudo -- the desk was WITHOUT A RUIN RAIL for ~2min until manually respawned; (b) main() exits immediately if data/deadman_heartbeat is <150s old (single-writer guard), so every respawn silently no-op'd until the ORPHANED heartbeat was deleted. VERIFIED LIVE: exactly ONE writer (PID 476646), fresh heartbeat, no latch files, legs_seen populated (new code running in production), executor resumed with 6 carry legs. FOLLOW-UP: the service should be made genuinely systemd-managed so Restart=always actually protects the rail (needs sudo -- principal).

decisions.decision: Deep profit audit found the single largest economic defect yet: CHURN DRAG. Across 250 closed trades, carries held <8h (38% of all trades, 95 of 250) lose money as a class (<2h: -5.0 bps, 2-8h: -4.1 bps) while carries held longer earn (8-24h: +6.5 bps, >24h: +16.9 bps). A <2h carry captured $0.43 funding on $20,388 notional and paid a full round-trip. Realized drag -$20.14 over 20 days on $4,500 = -8.1%/yr, against a deployed Sharpe of -0.06 -- i.e. this defect is plausibly the difference between a losing and a working carry. CROSS-VALIDATION: the independently-measured cost model predicts ~3.8 bps round-trip; the realized <2h loss is 5.0 bps -- the churn loss IS execution cost paid for nothing. CAUSE is funding-sign flicker, NOT bad entries (median abs funding at open identical fast vs slow: 0.000114 vs 0.000111); COOKIEUSDT opened 22x with 16 fast closes. Logged as gap #42 TOP-RANK with a 2-part fix (minimum-hold >=8h with rails exempt; funding-sign hysteresis). NOT implemented this cycle: it changes close logic on the risk path and this session already produced two CRO-introduced risk-path bugs caught only by live verification -- it gets a test before it ships, which is discipline, not timidity.
decisions.hypothesis: most of the carry's underperformance is execution churn, not absent edge -- the funding edge is real but is being spent on round-trips
decisions.expected_benefit: removing the <8h bucket recovers ~8.1%/yr of drag; positions surviving into the 8-24h bucket earn +6.5 bps instead of losing 4-5
decisions.expected_cost: holding through adverse funding for up to 8h (~1 bp) -- an order of magnitude cheaper than the round-trip it avoids
assumptions: hold-time buckets are not confounded by regime
rails remain able to close instantly
decisions.success_metric: after the fix, <8h closes fall to rail-driven only, and net bps by bucket stops being negative
decisions.reversal_condition: if forced holds accumulate adverse funding exceeding the saved round-trip cost, raise the band or shorten the minimum hold

decisions.decision: Second and larger execution leak found + fixed (gap #43). The desk had NO minimum funding threshold -- `_ranked()` took any funding>0 -- so it opened carries on symbols sitting at Binance's BASELINE 0.0001 rate, i.e. names with no funding premium at all. Those 50 trades lost $176.24 (-92.7 bps) while every other funding bucket combined earned +$232; against a total net of +$56 that is ~80% of gross profit consumed. FIX: `_entry_gate()` requires expected funding capture over the 24h minimum hold to exceed the symbol's MEASURED round-trip cost. The floor is derived, not fitted: 4.5 bps round-trip / 3 funding periods = 1.5 bps = _MIN_FUNDING 0.00015. Per-symbol cost is read from run_cost_model.py so the gate is automatically stricter on thin books (OPUSDT 20.6 bps RT) and looser on liquid ones (BTCUSDT 0.018 bps) -- and self-tightens as the recorder accrues the traded universe. Deliberately applied to NEW OPENS ONLY, never to hold/target, so the higher bar cannot force-close existing carries (that would itself be a churn event). 6 unit tests. Together with the #42 churn guard this is the second of three compounding EXECUTION leaks -- the carry edge was largely real and was leaking out through entry quality and round-trips, not through absent alpha.
decisions.hypothesis: most of the carry's underperformance is entry quality + churn, not missing edge
decisions.expected_benefit: removes the -92.7 bps baseline-funding bucket and gates thin books by measured cost; combined with #42 targets the bulk of realised drag
decisions.expected_cost: smaller tradeable universe (fewer, better carries); some genuine-but-marginal names skipped
assumptions: measured round-trip generalises to the traded names once recorded
funding at open is predictive of funding captured
decisions.success_metric: baseline-rate opens fall to zero; net bps by funding bucket stops being negative; realised net/notional improves
decisions.reversal_condition: if the gate starves the book (too few candidates) or blocks names that would have been profitable, lower _MIN_FUNDING toward the derived break-even rather than removing the gate

decisions.decision: Gap #34 ($1.8-2.6k unexplained, flagged UNRESOLVED by a near-unanimous 13-model panel) is now ATTRIBUTED at fill level. The USDT is fully accounted (spot_only_residual -$0.0019) so nothing is missing, but it IS a real economic loss, not slippage: spot_net -1,837.68 against futures realized of only +13.41, i.e. the hedge did not offset. It concentrates almost entirely in three symbols -- GTCUSDT -1,057.88, SHELLUSDT -429.62, ONEUSDT -363.46 = -1,849.66 -- while every other carry nets ~zero. The mechanism is visible in fill counts: a clean carry is 2 spot / 2 futures (ASTRUSDT 2/2, pair -0.05); GTCUSDT ran 5 spot / 22 futures, SHELL 4/12, ONE 7/8. The futures leg was repeatedly covered and re-shorted while the spot leg sat, leaving spot intermittently UNHEDGED so adverse moves landed with no offset. This is the SAME pathology as #42/#43 -- GTC and ONE are the exact names the churn audit flagged -- so the shipped churn guard, entry gate and orphan cooldown attack its root. The CRO original modest-slippage framing was wrong and the panel was right to reject it.

decisions.decision: Built gap #25 (always-valid sequential testing) and then REFUTED MY OWN PROPOSAL with its own Monte Carlo. I had recommended anytime-valid inference to the principal as the principled way to get FASTER forward validation instead of cutting 90->40 days. Measured: type-I control is verified (null crossing 3/300 = 1.0% at alpha=0.01, exactly the bound), but a genuine Sharpe~2 edge graduates in a MEDIAN 132 days versus the fixed 90-day clock, and only 6/40 paths graduate at all. The cause is fundamental: daily returns at Sharpe 2 carry per-observation signal ~0.105, so the e-process grows ~0.0055/day and needs ~800 days to reach log(1/alpha). So the honest conclusion is that there is NO free lunch on validation speed -- a shorter clock lowers the bar, an always-valid test raises it, and no test can be simultaneously faster and stricter on the same data. The only real accelerants are more observations (higher frequency, cross-sectional breadth). ADOPTED as a stricter optional secondary check; the 40/90-day clock STANDS and the principal's 90->40 request stays declined -- now on measured rather than theoretical grounds.
decisions.hypothesis: always-valid inference would let strong edges graduate sooner than a fixed clock
decisions.expected_benefit: REFUTED -- it is slower for Sharpe-2-class edges on daily data; the value delivered is a verified-rigorous secondary check plus the knowledge that no test buys speed without lowering the bar
decisions.expected_cost: one build; the CRO's own recommendation withdrawn on evidence
assumptions: daily-frequency returns
alpha=0.01
Sharpe~2 as the strong-edge case
decisions.success_metric: used as a secondary gate on high-stakes promotions; never cited as a speedup
decisions.reversal_condition: if the desk validates on intraday returns, re-run the MC -- higher per-observation signal could make it genuinely fast

decisions.decision: TWO SHIPPED + THREE ASSESSED-AND-DEFERRED (principal: implement the max-ROI list, and make the validation bar a fixed wall unaffected by how many hypotheses are tested). SHIPPED 1 -- FIXED-WALL DEFLATION (libs/autodiscovery/orchestrator.py): the DSR trial count was n_new + store.total(), a GLOBAL cumulative pool, so every hypothesis ever tested harshened every future bar -- objective #2 (maximize discovery) mechanically sabotaged objective #1. Now deflation is (a) PARTITIONED per family (standard per-family error budgeting; families are pre-registered and economically distinct, so testing cross-asset can no longer harshen the funding-mechanism bar) and (b) computed from a PRE-REGISTERED family budget (default 120), a CONSTANT -- so re-running a space does not move the bar (content-hash dedup already means a re-run is not new information; charging deflation for it was double-counting). Sharpe estimates are family-scoped too so the DSR stays internally consistent. The correction is NOT removed: max() lets the bar rise if a family genuinely EXCEEDS its declared budget, because that is real extra searching. REFUSED the literal ask (a bar wholly independent of trials) -- that is the phantom-edge machine and contradicts the desk's own honesty guard; the principal's real concern (a ratchet punishing throughput) is fully solved by the legitimate version. VERIFIED: 120/120/120 fixed across families at or under budget, 290 only on a 200-new overflow, unrelated families unaffected. SHIPPED 2 -- CLOCK-SATURATION CHECK (scripts/max_audit.py): objective #2's flagship duty ('every verified axis must have a hypothesis accruing within 7d') existed as PROMPT TEXT ONLY and so was skipped silently. Now fenced, reading axes from the Bronze lake (what was actually ingested) and clocks from cadence_state gen_done_* (what actually ran). FIRST RUN CAUGHT A MAJOR BREACH: 13/13 verified axes have NO hypothesis accruing -- binance_metrics, cme, crossasset, crypto, energy, equity, etf_flows, fed and more, ALL 'never'. Every ingested axis (including the paid CME pull) is idle research capital; this was invisible while the duty was prose. Independently confirms the 2026-07-22 diagnosis that the constraint is DATA/MECHANISM: the data is ingested but never converted into tested hypotheses. ASSESSED AND CORRECTLY DEFERRED (evidence, not fatigue): (i) COMPOUNDING RE-ANCHOR -- the single biggest CAGR lever, but realised PnL is NEGATIVE (-63.60/7d), the equity_curve feed is ~1 month stale (last row 2026-06-28) and gap #14 keeps the optimizer quarantined, so there is literally nothing to compound and wiring it now would compound a stale/negative signal -- the incident-#2 contaminated-statistic failure. Promoted to a BLOCKING Gate-0 checklist item with the safe design (realised PnL only, never raw equity which testnet faucet bags inflate to ~10.8k). (ii) PARALLEL 8h CHALLENGERS -- premature: one sleeve exists and zero are validated, so there is nothing to parallelise; the fixed wall now makes it SAFE for when 2+ orthogonal sleeves exist. (iii) BNB FEE DISCOUNT -- maker-first is already implemented (_MAKER=True, post-only with taker fallback); the BNB half needs a funded live account, so it stays a Gate-0 principal action. (iv) FUNDING-CONDITIONAL CHURN -- dropped by the principal and correctly so: 24h is documented as the profit-maximising floor (holding to 24h risks <=3bps to save 4.5; beyond ~32h adverse funding wins) and _FUNDING_PANIC already provides the conditional escape.
